contents.entry: Mechanism: plan seed, ledger rows, panel frame
The data model carried from the execution rail
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
State paths and their cleanup scripts
The Krastorio look of the rail

pointers.sibling: JSON schema of plan.step, plan.side, ledger.row and rail.panel
Bearings page service: the panel lives on the page
Status code map loader: the plan's status codes come from the plan XML the same way
Spec book check validates the plan XML the rail is generated from
pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: The rail panel shows any numbered plan on the owner's page: the current step and its last line, a progress bar, the rail of steps with their status codes, the ledger newest first, and the side panels the plan supplies, folded closed; it moves only when a ledger row lands.
purpose.is-not: It is not a second surface, not a claude.ai artifact, and has no publish step; the plan document stays the source of truth and the panel is its view.
purpose.why: The execution rail (owner's locked tracker, 2026-09-21) is the right data model and the wrong surface: it needed a manual republish after every ledger row, lived on a claude.ai URL the owner's standard refuses for status, and broke the global rule that bearings is the only visual surface (D20, L11 F2). Ruled on C51: the rail's plan and ledger become a bearings panel the system writes.
purpose.decisions: D20 C (C51), D21 push (C52), D24 repo truth (C54), D10 one store (K07 no two sources of truth), the look rule.

record.field: the plan id (rebuild for the Factory Rebuild Plan; any later plan has its own)
the step id (R-01 and so on)
started, complete, blocked, issue, question, checkpoint (the execution rail's set)
who wrote it (a node, a seat, the architect, the owner)
an optional URL or record id

input.text: A ledger row is written by the CLI coq ledger <plan> <step> <status> "<text>" [ref] (which replaces bin/ledger.sh of the rail skill) or by a node that ends a step (N-51 exit verdict, N-48 promotion). It reaches this node pushed (N-31). The plan's steps are seeded as plan.step records (mechanism step 1), which the panel also receives pushed.

record.field: the first step with no complete row, and its last row
every step with its state code: not-started, running, blocked, done, superseded (the plan's own codes), derived from its rows
rows newest first, capped at ledger_window (config, 200)
the side panels (status code map, build mode, failure cases, recovery) from plan.side
whether the plan's signal row (default GOTEAM) exists

output.text: rail.panel is a frame inside the page (derived, not stored as a record of its own, the same rule as N-31's frames); the panel is rendered by the page from plan.step, plan.side and ledger.row records applied by (kind, key, version), so there is nothing to publish and nothing that can drift from the records.

mechanism.where: Go service (D01), package internal/owner/rail for the seed and the ledger CLI; the panel markup is a section of tools/bearings/assets/page.html with its own fold; plan generation stays in rebuild/bin/plan-to-rail.sh (reads factory-rebuild-plan.xml, writes plan.json and side.html, refuses on drift with --check).
mechanism.step: Seed: on coq.service start and on Reload (N-43 shape), the service reads every plan registered in tools/bearings/config/plans.json (id, plan.json path, side.html path, signal) from the checkout, validates plan.json against the rail's shape (ordered array of {id, t, who, gate, owner}) and upserts one plan.step record per step keyed plan:<plan>:<step> (compare-and-swap; unchanged steps produce no write) and one plan.side record per plan with the side HTML. A plan file that fails validation writes plan.invalid 400 and the last good seed stays.

Ledger: coq ledger validates the step exists in the seeded plan, the status is one of the six, the text is fifteen words or fewer and carries no em dash, then Store.Put a ledger.row with idempotency key ledger:<plan>:<step>:<at>:<hash of text> and prints the same line the writer pastes to the owner. The TSV file of the rail skill becomes an export (coq ledger export --plan rebuild > ledger.tsv), never a source (K07).

Derive: the step state is a pure function of its rows: no row is not-started; a started row with no complete is running; a blocked row after the last started is blocked; a complete row is done; a superseded row (owner only) is superseded. The panel computes it client-side from the pushed rows, and the service computes the same for the health line (N-06) with one shared function, tested for equality.

Render: the page's rail section draws the frame from its applied state on every frame that touches plan.* or ledger.row for a plan it shows; a plan selector lists seeded plans; the fold state is remembered per browser.

Approval: a ledger row with status checkpoint and text equal to the plan's signal (GOTEAM default; GOFACTORY for the rebuild) by the owner (source: a ruling from N-29 with effect gofactory, which writes the row) sets approved; the top card stops saying the plan is waiting. No --approved flag, no marker file.
mechanism.text: Why the rail stays one data model: the owner locked it on 2026-09-21 and uses it; only the surface and the publish step were wrong. plan.json, side.html, the six statuses, fifteen words, the rail-left ledger-right layout above 1000 px and one column on the phone are all kept.

data-model.plan-step: {id, t, who, gate, owner} per rebuild/plan.json, generated from the XML by plan-to-rail.sh; id pattern letter-dash-two-digits (R-01, E-01).
data-model.ledger-row: {at_utc, step, status, text, by, ref} per the rail skill's TSV columns, now a record.
data-model.side: a list of {title, html} folds generated from the plan XML (status code map, build mode rule, failure cases, recovery), stored as plan.side; never hand-written (plan-to-rail.sh comment).
data-model.signal: the approval word, GOTEAM by default, GOFACTORY for the rebuild plan; matched exactly on a checkpoint row by the owner.

start.text: Seeding runs inside coq.service at start and on Reload; the panel is part of the page the unit serves (N-32). Nothing is typed. The node ships dark behind rail.enabled; its go-live proof is the rebuild plan seeded on dev, a ledger row written by the CLI appearing in the panel within one frame, and rebuild/rail.sh retired with the artifact URL's last row saying so.

wait.what: plan file read and validate at seed
wait.fallback: plan.invalid 400 with the reason; the last good seed stays; a fix is a pull request
retry 3 times (1, 2, 4 s); then rail.seed.failed 500 and the next Reload retries; the panel shows the last seeded version with its built_at
retry 3 times; then exit 4 with the row printed so the writer can re-run; the row is idempotent by key so a re-run after a late commit is a no-op

wait.what: a ledger row arriving at the page
wait.fallback: the page's staleness state covers a stalled stream (N-32); the rail shows built_at so a stale rail is visible

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node was a human republishing a page after every row; it is gone. The remaining wait is the store, bounded and reported as above.

retries.rule: Seed and ledger writes retry 3 times with backoff then report; Reload and the level-triggered seed on every service start are the recovery; every write is idempotent by key.

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume; any number of seats and nodes write ledger rows at once.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets touch internal/owner/rail, the coq ledger verb, tools/bearings/config/plans.json, the rail section of page.html (one ticket, since page.html is one file) and the tests; plan-to-rail.sh belongs to the rebuild tooling already on main.

collision.what: two writers append ledger rows for the same step in the same second

many-agents-at-once.collision: Both commit (append-only, distinct keys by text hash); the panel shows both in seq order; the derived state uses the latest by seq, which is the store's order, so two readers never disagree.

collision.what: two seeds at once (a Reload during a start)

many-agents-at-once.collision: Upserts by key with compare-and-swap; identical content produces no write; a changed plan.json wins by version. plan.json itself is one file edited by one ticket at a time and generated from the XML, so two seeds never carry different truths.

collision.what: a ledger row for a step the plan no longer has

many-agents-at-once.collision: Refused by the CLI with exit 3 naming the step; a node's row for a removed step writes ledger.rejected 400 as an alert (the plan changed under a running step, which only the owner may do).
Each plan has its own key space; the page shows one at a time with a selector; frames are filtered by the plans the page lists.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests write 50 rows from 5 writers under the fake clock and assert the derived state on the service and on the page are equal and that every row is present once.

emits.acts: the page draws; N-06 derives; a blocked row with the owner's plan is owner-acts through N-28

status-codes.emits: a row for an unknown step or over fifteen words
status-codes.text: The mapping of the six rail statuses onto the HTTP-shaped codes is a row the shared author adds; the five plan step states (not-started, running, blocked, done, superseded) stay the plan XML's own and are derived, never written.

path.what: in N-01; kept for the life of the store (the plan's history is the owner's record)
path.cleanup: registered with N-45 as store retention class owner-surface; a retired plan's rows are exported then removed by coq ledger retire --plan <id> --dry-run, then --yes

path.what: the rail skill's outputs; ledger.tsv is imported once as ledger.row records (coq ledger import --dry-run then --yes, counts match), then the three files are cleanup targets

path.p: exports: coq ledger export writes where the caller says
path.what: never under the repository; the caller's path
path.cleanup: kept on purpose: an export belongs to whoever asked for it (the owner's CLI); nothing of the system's lives there
none: tracked source, removed by a pull request

edges.writes-via: coq ledger and the seed write records
edges.reads: a ruling with effect gofactory writes the approval row

look.rule: The rail panel is a Factorio GUI frame on the page: the step rail as a vertical belt of slot-size 40 tiles, each tile a lamp in the plan's state colour (not-started unlit grey, running orange #FAA838, blocked heat red #DA4535, done production green #2BE327, superseded dimmed with the caption colour), the progress bar as production_progressbar 24 px high in #2BE327 on #3E3D3E, the current step as a subheader_frame 36 px high with caption #FFE6C0, the ledger as rows in inside_shallow_frame #403F40 with the status word in count-font and the fifteen words in body white, side folds as tooltip-style frames #1F1E1F at 88 percent. Font Titillium Web; figures mono. One column on the phone at 430 CSS px; rail left and ledger right above 1000 px (the rail's own breakpoint, kept). No Wube or BiusArt pixel.
look.check: Playwright asserts the lamp colour per derived state and the layout at both widths; screenshots go to the owner before the uat confirm card.

permissions.runs-as: inside coq.service for the seed; the CLI as the caller's seat identity
permissions.may: any seat or node may write a ledger row for a step it works on (by is the socket identity, never a free field); the owner's signal row is written only by a ruling (N-29)
permissions.may-not: no seat may write plan.step or plan.side (the seed does, from the repository); no one hand-edits the panel markup outside the look ticket; superseded is the owner's alone

gauge.on: N-40; the time bound check of factory-rebuild-plan.xml failure case stall reads this

runbook.op: coq ledger rebuild R-03 started "Spec book volumes being written by seven author seats"
add a row to tools/bearings/config/plans.json pointing at its plan.json and side.html, make lint, pull request; coq reload seeds it
only the owner adds or removes steps (factory-rebuild-plan.xml change rule); edit the XML, run plan-to-rail.sh, pull request; the seed follows
rebuild/bin/cleanup-rail-state.sh --dry-run then --yes after the import; coq ledger retire for a finished plan
runbook.cost: A seed step in the service and a plan registry file; the rail's claude.ai page stops being updated, which the owner ruled.
